Yoshinori Kanada
Various

'A Standard-Bearer of Anime's Third Generation' (Animage)
His distinctive movement and timing, his deformed character designs, the shapes of his explosions and beams, and the way he presented robots left a huge influence on countless animators who came after him.
Even Mr. Ochi and Mr. Nabeshima, who these days feel firmly rooted in directing, were once drawing key animation with real gusto back in the day.
There's probably a growing generation that has no idea about any of this, but even 'the' Mutsumi Inomata and Masayuki were influenced by Kanada as well. (Well, in Masayuki's case, it could be said he was influenced more strongly -- and thus only indirectly -- by Masahito Yamashita and Kazuhide Tomonaga.)
These days there are far fewer chances to see his work, but there's plenty of it available on packaged video media, so anyone who feels like it can enjoy as much as they want. Anyone interested should go look for it themselves.
